correctness.rationale: The Brownian-bridge conditional integral-variance identity yields the exact cubic-gap functional, and its interval-emptiness representation supplies a nonnegative signed-measure quadratic form. The normalized candidate density has constant potential on its interior support and a strict quadratic obstacle outside. Expansion against any Borel competitor proves global optimality; equality of interval-mass differences and the unit interior mass prove uniqueness even with atoms or endpoints. Exact moment calculation gives the risk; a standalone symbolic/exact-rational/high-precision verifier confirms critical finite and algebraic identities. Limits are two iid noiseless nodes and the E[sup] RKHS posterior variance objective.

value.rationale: Choosing a node proposal in kernel quadrature is a motivated design question. The first nontrivial independent-node case has a genuinely nonuniform, compact-central-support optimum with a sharp root defining its support, unique among all Borel laws, and a 35.8 percent reduction in expected posterior integral uncertainty versus uniform sampling. This exact benchmark can test adaptive and learned proposal-design algorithms and exposes a meaningful sampling-versus-deterministic design distinction; no general larger-n theorem is claimed.
